summary.title: Face clustering with Python
summary.one_liner: You learn how to group unlabeled face images into per-person clusters by encoding faces as 128-d vectors with the face_recognition library and clustering them with DBSCAN in Python.
keywords: find unique faces in image dataset
how to count unique people in photos
takeaways: Face clustering is unsupervised: you group faces without names or labels, unlike face recognition, which is supervised.
Encode each detected face as a 128-d feature vector with face_recognition, then store the encodings in a pickle file.
Use DBSCAN rather than k-means when the number of people is unknown, since DBSCAN finds clusters from point density and marks outliers as -1.
Build per-cluster image montages with imutils to visually check whether each cluster holds one person.
On the 129-image soccer dataset, DBSCAN produced five clusters, with one Messi image left as an outlier.
summary.summary: The post, inspired by a reader question, explains face clustering as finding the unique people in an unlabeled set of images, with a law-enforcement example as motivation. It uses two Python scripts: encode_faces.py detects faces (HOG or CNN) and writes 128-d encodings to a pickle file, and cluster_faces.py runs scikit-learn DBSCAN on those encodings and shows a montage of faces for each cluster. The worked example uses 129 photos of five famous soccer players, producing five clusters with one image left as an outlier. The author notes Chinese whispers as an alternative for very large datasets.
